label: input token l at original positions 2-6
explanation: Fires only when the input token is l during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at positions 2 through 6. Covers 32% of all l inputs and essentially all activation mass. It never fires on any other token, at positions 0-1, at positions 7-8 (2 tiny exceptions in dev), on the delimiter, or in the copy phase, even when l is fed back as a copy input. Magnitude is weak at t=2: 15k activations there hold only 5% of mass. It is strongest at t=3-5. It is lower on repeated l (in_first=0 holds 13% of mass on 12% of activations, and a second l in a sequence is usually weaker). Top examples often have n or 1 earlier in the prefix, but that was not checked quantitatively. False positives (about 2.5%) are mostly l at t=2 that stays inactive.

issues: I could not refute the claims. Test split: precision 0.976, recall 0.99995, F1 0.988, mass recall 0.999997. Only 3 activations were missed, all l at t=7 with activations of 0.02-0.04 relative to max, holding 0.0% of the mass.

Confirmed 'never fires in the copy phase': (phase==2)&(in_tok==l) has precision 0.0 over 91k steps. The dev profile shows zero activations at the delimiter, at t=0-1, at t>=8, and on any token other than l.
Confirmed the hard positional cutoff: l at t>=7 has precision 0.0002 (2 of 8229 steps). On l, the firing rate is flat at about 0.033 for original positions 2-6.

The false positives sit almost entirely at t=2. l at t=2 has precision 0.912, against 0.996 for l at t=3-6. They look like scattered near-threshold noise, not a systematic class. Precision at t=2 barely moves when split by L (3: 0.905, 4: 0.913, >=5: 0.912), by a vowel as prev_tok (0.912), by a digit at orig(0) or orig(1) (0.93), or by whether l was seen earlier (0.910). This matches the low mass share at t=2 (5.4%).

The repeated-l claim checks out only partly. Firing precision is not lower for in_first==0 (0.989) than for in_first==1 (0.973). The stated lower magnitude for repeated l was not verified, since score reports only firing, and it is a minor claim. The 'n or 1 earlier in the prefix' observation was admitted as unchecked and is not part of the predicate.
The label matches the predicate exactly and does not overclaim.
